goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: getCredentials() re-creates the credential model on every read with a fresh random ID and hash, so updateStoredCredential or deletion by that credential ID targets a nonexistent ID and silently fails
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: the credential model returned by getCredentials() does not preserve the stored credential’s ID, so downstream operations that rely on that ID (update/delete via stored credential ID, e.g., removeStoredCredentialById) will fail. The golden says the ID is null if not set; the candidate says it’s regenerated/random, but in both cases the returned ID doesn’t match the persisted one.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Used recovery codes are likely never consumed for user-storage users because updateCredential requires a UserCredentialModel with remaining codes but the authenticator uses the local-storage path (updateStoredCredential), which no-ops or throws for federated users, leaving leaked recovery codes replayable forever

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows creation and lookup changes for recovery codes in federated user storage (CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential uses user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...) first; RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(...) prefers federated credentials via getFederatedCredentialsStream()). The finding’s core claim—that the authenticator consumes codes via a local-storage-only path like updateStoredCredential which no-ops/throws for federated users—is not evidenced anywhere in the shown diff (no consumption/update-after-use logic is present). While the test user-storage provider’s isValid() checks codes without consuming them, that is separate from the claimed authenticator/local-storage consumption mismatch and cannot confirm the stated defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getCredentials() re-creates the credential model on every read with a fresh random ID and hash, so updateStoredCredential or deletion by that credential ID targets a nonexistent ID and silently fails
matched_golden_ids: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: the credential model returned by getCredentials() does not preserve the stored credential’s ID, so downstream operations that rely on that ID (update/delete via stored credential ID, e.g., removeStoredCredentialById) will fail. The golden says the ID is null if not set; the candidate says it’s regenerated/random, but in both cases the returned ID doesn’t match the persisted one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deserialization failure (IOException) in getCredentials() is swallowed and returns a stream without the recovery credential, masking the storage error and making the user appear to have no recovery codes

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`, recovery codes are deserialized with `JsonSerialization.readValue(...)` inside a `try` and on `IOException` it only logs (`log.error(...)`) and continues, returning a stream without the recovery-codes credential (while still returning OTP if present). This indeed can mask a storage/serialization problem and make the user appear to have no recovery codes, but it’s in a testsuite user storage provider and only affects the error/corrupt-data path rather than being a clear functional defect introduced for valid data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent fallback to local storage when updateCredential() returns false can create a second, divergent credential, causing user to be shown one set of codes but validated against another

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` only creates a local (Keycloak DB) credential when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` returns `false` (i.e., the user storage did not accept/update it). When it returns `true`, it does not create a local credential. In the fallback case, the local credential is created from the same `credentialModel` derived from the same `generatedCodes`, so the diff does not show a path where the user is shown one set of codes but validation uses a different, divergent stored set. A “second credential despite false return” would require a misbehaving user storage provider, which is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plaintext recovery codes are shipped to user storage (stored and compared raw) while local storage stores only hashes, changing the security contract and risking code leakage or validation failure depending on provider convention

adjudication.rationale: The new `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` serializes `generatedCodes` (raw recovery codes) to JSON and passes it as the `challengeResponse` in a `UserCredentialModel` to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. This explicitly ships plaintext recovery codes into user storage implementations. The added test user storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`) then stores this raw JSON (`setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`) and validates by direct equality against `input.getChallengeResponse()`, confirming raw storage/compare semantics. This is a security regression for federated/user storage: recovery codes become retrievable in plaintext by the storage provider, and providers expecting hashed/opaque data could mis-handle validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean still calls .get() on an Optional without a presence check, producing a raw NoSuchElementException/500 error instead of graceful failure when no credential exists in either storage

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the diff changes credential lookup to `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` but then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. Since `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can return `Optional.empty()` when the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage, this will throw `NoSuchElementException` at runtime (likely resulting in a 500) rather than failing gracefully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NPE on unknown user in the new federated branches of updateCredential because users.get(...).recoveryCodes dereferences without a null check, defeating the fallback-to-local logic in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential

adjudication.rationale: In the new RecoveryAuthnCodes branch of BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential, the code does `users.get(translateUserName(user.getUsername())).recoveryCodes = recoveryCodesModel;` without checking for null, so if the map lookup ever returns null it would NPE and would indeed prevent CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential from falling back to local storage. However, the diff does not show that `updateCredential` is ever called for an “unknown user” in this provider, and the existing OTP branch already had the same pattern (`users.get(...).otp = ...`), suggesting the provider assumes the user exists. So this is a robustness/edge-case concern, not a verifiable newly introduced failing bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext (unhashed) via challengeResponse in createRecoveryCodesCredential, allowing custom storages to persist recoverable plaintext secrets that leak usable 2FA codes if the storage DB is compromised

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly serializes the newly generated recovery codes (`generatedCodes`) to JSON and puts them into `UserCredentialModel` as the credential's `challengeResponse` (`new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`) before calling `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`. This sends the raw (usable) recovery codes to any user storage provider implementing `updateCredential`. The added test user storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`) persists `input.getChallengeResponse()` directly into `CredentialModel.credentialData` and later validates by deserializing and doing a plaintext equality check, confirming the codes are stored recoverably. That is a concrete security weakness: compromise of the user storage DB would reveal valid 2FA recovery codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls .get() on an Optional from RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without a presence check, causing NoSuchElementException and a 500 error during login when the credential is missing

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the constructor now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` with no presence check. `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can legitimately return `Optional.empty()` if the user has no recovery-codes credential in federated or local storage, which would throw `NoSuchElementException` and can translate to a 500 during page rendering/login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage isValid never invalidates consumed recovery codes, allowing indefinite replay of the same code and weakening the one-time-use guarantee

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the new Recovery Codes branch only deserializes the stored JSON list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without updating/removing the matched code from `myUser.recoveryCodes` (or otherwise persisting consumption). As implemented in this diff, a valid recovery code remains in the stored list indefinitely, enabling replay for users backed by this user storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() enumerates the user's full credential set twice per lookup, streaming all federated credentials unfiltered on the hot path instead of using a targeted getCredentialByType-style query

adjudication.rationale: In the added `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` method, the lookup first iterates `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and filters by type, and if not found it performs a second lookup via `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(TYPE)`. This can require scanning all federated credentials (and potentially doing two traversals/queries per call when the federated credential is absent). That’s a performance/hot-path concern, but not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() re-deserializes the recovery-codes JSON and reallocates the credential list on every call, causing repeated parse work per authentication transaction

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials()` the method allocates a new `ArrayList` each call and, when `myUser.recoveryCodes != null`, re-parses the JSON every time via `JsonSerialization.readValue(myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData(), List.class)` to rebuild a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded inefficiency (repeated work per invocation), but it does not constitute a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plaintext recovery codes passed via `updateCredential` to user storage providers, causing unhashed secrets to be persisted at rest

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which serializes the *raw* `generatedCodes` list to JSON (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and passes it to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` via `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`. For user storage providers, `updateCredential` receives this value as `input.getChallengeResponse()`. The updated `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential(...)` persists it directly (`recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`) and validation compares plaintext values (`generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`). This demonstrates plaintext recovery codes being passed into and stored by user storage providers, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated recovery codes are never consumed/invalidated after successful use, allowing indefinite reuse

adjudication.rationale: In the federated user storage implementation added/updated in this diff, recovery codes are validated but never consumed. Specifically, `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` deserializes the stored JSON list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without removing the matched code or updating the stored credential afterwards. With `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` persisting the codes as a plain JSON list into user storage via `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`, nothing in the shown changes performs invalidation after a successful use, enabling reuse of the same federated recovery code indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded literal provider ID string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" replaces the PROVIDER_ID constant, risking drift on rename

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` the provider is looked up with a hardcoded string: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. The diff also shows previous usage of a constant provider id (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID`) being removed from `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction`. While the hardcoded value may currently match the actual provider id, this change creates a concrete maintenance/rename drift risk grounded in the diff, not an immediately verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Optional.get()` called without presence check in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean, throwing NoSuchElementException when credential absent

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the diff changes to `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking `isPresent()`. If the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage (i.e., `getCredential` returns `Optional.empty()`), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getCredential` silently changes precedence to federated-over-local, undocumented behavioral change for existing callers

adjudication.rationale: The new `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` explicitly checks federated credentials first (`getFederatedCredentialsStream() ... findFirst()`) and only falls back to local (`getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`). Existing callers in this diff were previously reading only local credentials (e.g., `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` used `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst()`), so if a user ever has both a federated and a local recovery-codes credential, the chosen credential now changes to “federated wins” without any caller-visible documentation beyond the new method’s Javadoc. This is a real behavioral/precedence change, but not verifiably a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() on an Optional without isPresent() check, causing NoSuchElementException/HTTP 500 when no recovery-codes credential is resolvable

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the code now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. If `getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()` (no federated or stored recovery-codes credential), this will throw `NoSuchElementException`, which can surface as an HTTP 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential passes raw unhashed recovery codes via UserCredentialModel.setChallengeResponse() to user-storage providers, leaking plaintext credentials to third-party storage

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the code serializes `generatedCodes` (raw recovery codes) to JSON and builds `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`, then calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)`. This passes the plaintext recovery codes via the credential input's challenge response to any user-storage provider that supports updating credentials. The diff also updates a user-storage implementation (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`) to persist `input.getChallengeResponse()` directly as `credentialData`, confirming the raw JSON is what gets stored. This is a security-sensitive credential and the method ignores the provided `credentialModel` (which may contain the properly processed/hashed form) for the user-storage path, making the finding verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes are never consumed or invalidated in the user-storage path, allowing indefinite replay of single-use codes

adjudication.rationale: In the user-storage implementation added for recovery codes, validation does not consume/disable a used code. `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without removing the matched code or updating stored credential data, allowing the same recovery code to be replayed indefinitely in the federated/user-storage path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded provider lookup string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" with no null check, causing NullPointerException if the provider is missing or feature is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the provider is looked up via `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")` and the result is used without a null check (`recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`). If the provider is not registered/available (e.g., feature disabled or misconfigured), this will throw a `NullPointerException`. The hardcoded string is also introduced by this diff, increasing the risk of a mismatch with the actual provider id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error swallowing in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials: IOException logged and silently returns stream without the recovery-codes credential, hiding the root cause

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials`, the new recovery-codes branch catches `IOException` from `JsonSerialization.readValue(...)`, logs only a generic error message (`log.error("Could not deserialize  credential of type: recovery-codes")`) and then continues returning a stream without adding the recovery-codes credential. This does swallow the exception and can mask data/serialization problems (especially since the stack trace isn’t logged), but it’s not fully “silent” because an error is logged, and the behavior (omitting an unreadable credential) may be an intentional fallback for this testsuite provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IOException in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential wrapped in bare RuntimeException with no message or user/realm context

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, JSON serialization of `generatedCodes` is wrapped in `try/catch` and on failure it does `throw new RuntimeException(e);` with no explanatory message and no inclusion of user/realm/provider context (diff hunk adds `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` and the bare wrap). This is verifiably true from the diff. It’s primarily an error-handling/diagnostics concern rather than a guaranteed functional defect, since a serialization failure is exceptional and the code will still fail fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that a used recovery code is invalidated after successful login on the federated storage path; the federated isValid only does a membership check with no consumption

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds federated-storage support for recovery codes in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, but that implementation only deserializes the stored JSON list and checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without any visible consumption/invalidation logic. The newly added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` performs a single successful login using a recovery code, but does not attempt a second login reusing the same code to assert one-time-use semantics on the federated path. This is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap for the new federated recovery-codes behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The userStorage-fallback branch of CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (when updateCredential returns false) is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new branching logic in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`: it first calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` and only if that returns false does it fall back to `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)`. The newly added integration test `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` configures a federated user storage that explicitly supports `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` and whose `updateCredential(...)` implementation returns `true` for that type, and it asserts the credential exists in user storage and not in DB. Nothing in the diff adds a test case that forces `updateCredential` to return false to exercise the fallback-to-local-storage branch, so that specific branch is not covered by the added tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative-path test for invalid recovery code during federated login, including the null-guard branch when storedRecoveryKeys is null

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new federated recovery-codes logic and a positive-path test (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest#testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin) that only covers successful setup and login. In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage#isValid, a new branch handles RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE and explicitly returns false when `storedRecoveryKeys` is null (with a warn log), and also returns false on JSON deserialization failure; none of the added tests exercise an invalid recovery code during federated login or the `storedRecoveryKeys == null` guard path. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing test for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for credential removal/disable for a federated user, leaving getCredentials/lifecycle surface untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new federated recovery-codes support and lifecycle surface in the user storage provider (e.g., `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`, `updateCredential(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, and `isConfiguredFor(...)`/`isValid(...)`). The newly added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` only covers setup + authentication and asserts the credential exists in user storage, but there is no analogous test exercising credential removal/disable flows for a federated user (unlike the existing OTP test that deletes the OTP credential via Account REST). Thus the provider’s credential lifecycle behavior for recovery codes (removal/disable and any `getCredentials` interaction after that) remains untested in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Storage-state assertions bypass the public credential API, coupling tests to internal static maps instead of the credential-manager path

adjudication.rationale: The new test assertion `assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage` calls `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes("otp1")`, which directly inspects the provider’s internal `userPasswords` map (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory#hasRecoveryCodes`). This verifies storage state via test-provider internals rather than going through the public credential path (`user.credentialManager()` / credential streams). That does couple the test to the provider’s internal representation and bypasses the credential-manager API (even though the codebase already does a similar thing for OTP via `hasUserOTP`). It’s a maintainability/architecture concern in the tests, not a functional defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The getCredentials IOException -> log.error -> silently omit credential branch is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new error-handling branch in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`: when `myUser.recoveryCodes != null`, it attempts `JsonSerialization.readValue(...)` and on `IOException` it logs `log.error("Could not deserialize  credential of type: recovery-codes")` and then proceeds without adding the recovery-codes credential to the returned stream (effectively omitting it). The newly added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` exercises the happy path (valid JSON) but does not cover the `IOException` path or assert behavior when deserialization fails. So the finding that this silent-omit branch is untested is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential precedence when user has both federated and local credentials, and the empty-case behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial selection logic in `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` that explicitly prefers a federated credential (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()...findFirst()`) and falls back to local storage (`getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`). Call sites were switched to this helper (e.g., `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` and `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`). The newly added integration test (`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`) only covers the case where recovery codes exist in user storage, and does not exercise (1) the precedence when both federated and local recovery-code credentials exist, nor (2) the empty-case (no credential found), which is especially relevant because `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean still calls .get() on the Optional, risking an untested NPE when no credential exists

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the new code obtains `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. If no recovery-codes credential exists, this will throw (NoSuchElementException, not NPE). The diff does not show that this constructor is only ever used when the credential must exist, so the risk is real but not conclusively a newly introduced, verifiable broken behavior from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test helpers hardcode username "otp1" instead of deriving the username from the userId parameter

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest`, helper methods accept a `userId` parameter but still hardcode the username `"otp1"` in multiple places (e.g., `setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction()` calls `testAppHelper.startLogin("otp1", "pass")`, and `assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage()` queries `storageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes("otp1")`). This isn’t a functional defect for the current test because the user is created as `"otp1"`, but it makes the helpers misleading/non-reusable and fragile if called with a different user in the future.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw (unhashed) recovery codes serialized to JSON and passed through credential plumbing in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, so the credential is stored hashed in one path and plaintext in the other, leaking plaintext codes to federated storages

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the raw `generatedCodes` list is serialized to JSON (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and put into a `UserCredentialModel` as the credential value (`new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`), then sent through `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` for the federated/user-storage path. The testsuite federated storage implementation (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`) persists `input.getChallengeResponse()` directly into `CredentialModel.credentialData` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, meaning the JSON of raw codes is stored in plaintext in federated storage. The fallback path uses `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` (without `generatedCodes`), implying different storage semantics between paths and, at minimum, a plaintext leak to federated storage introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Serialization format responsibility leaked into generic utility: external storage must know to JSON-parse getChallengeResponse() as List<String>, with no shared constant/schema for the wire format

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes a JSON wire format for recovery codes when writing to user storage: `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializes `generatedCodes` via `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` and stores it in `new UserCredentialModel(..., recoveryCodesJson)` (i.e., as the credential input/challengeResponse). The federated storage implementation then must know to persist `input.getChallengeResponse()` and later JSON-deserialize it back to a `List` (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential` and `getCredentials` use `JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class)`). This couples external/user storage implementations to an implicit serialization format without an explicit shared schema/constant in the diff. It’s an architectural/API-contract concern rather than an immediately verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Magic-string provider ID "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" hardcoded in CredentialHelper, which would silently break if the provider ID is renamed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which retrieves the provider via a hardcoded ID: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. This is diff-grounded and creates a maintainability/robustness issue versus using a shared constant (the removed code previously referenced `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID`). If the provider ID were ever renamed, this would likely return null and later fail at `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`, but the diff alone doesn’t prove an immediate functional break today.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper (generic SPI utility) is hard-coupled to one specific built-in credential provider, defeating the point of a generic helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, which directly hard-codes the recovery-codes provider id via `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")` and uses it to create the credential when user-storage update fails. This introduces a Keycloak-built-in, provider-specific dependency into `CredentialHelper` (a generic SPI utility), which is an architectural coupling concern rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls Optional.get() unconditionally, defeating the new Optional-returning lookup contract and still throwing NoSuchElementException on the 'no credential anywhere' case

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the code now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. If the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage, this will throw `NoSuchElementException`, despite the lookup being modeled as `Optional` in the new helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test-provider validation in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid compares plaintext recovery codes and never consumes/rotates used codes, diverging from the real single-use contract

adjudication.rationale: In the new RecoveryAuthnCodes branch of BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, the provider deserializes the stored JSON list and validates via `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, i.e., a plaintext equality check, and it does not remove/rotate the matched code or update `myUser.recoveryCodes` afterward. This makes recovery codes effectively reusable in this test user-storage implementation, which can diverge from Keycloak’s intended single-use behavior and reduce the fidelity of backwards-compatibility tests, but it’s confined to the testsuite provider code in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.enterRecoveryCodes takes EnterRecoveryAuthnCodePage and WebDriver as parameters despite the page being an injected @Page field, duplicating state and leaking driver-management into a business helper

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest, EnterRecoveryAuthnCodePage is already an injected @Page field (protected EnterRecoveryAuthnCodePage enterRecoveryAuthnCodePage;). However, the new helper method enterRecoveryCodes(EnterRecoveryAuthnCodePage enterRecoveryAuthnCodePage, WebDriver driver, ...) is called with that same field plus the raw driver and then manually does enterRecoveryAuthnCodePage.setDriver(driver). This duplicates state management and exposes WebDriver handling in what is otherwise a business-level test helper. It’s a maintainability/architecture concern in the added test code, not a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes statically shares provider state (userPasswords map), hard-coupling test assertions to implementation internals in a separation-of-concerns leak

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows a new helper method `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes` reading `userPasswords.get(username)` and a test calling it for an assertion. The finding’s key claim that this is “statically shared provider state” is not verifiable from the diff (we don’t see `userPasswords` declared as static or otherwise), and the added method is in a testsuite provider/factory used explicitly for test assertions, not production code. While the test is indeed coupled to the test provider’s internals, that appears intentional for the backwards-compatibility test harness rather than a concrete defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: value vs challengeResponse mismatch: createRecoveryCodesCredential sets the credential value but isValid compares challengeResponse, so credentials created in user storage can never validate while updateCredential returns true (silent-pass)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a verifiable “value vs challengeResponse” mismatch. `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` builds a `UserCredentialModel(..., credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)` and passes it to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. In the updated test user storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`), the credential is persisted using `input.getChallengeResponse()` (as `credentialData`), and validation (`isValid`) deserializes that stored `credentialData` and compares each stored code to `input.getChallengeResponse()` (the user-entered code). Nothing in the diff demonstrates that `UserCredentialModel` would populate a different field than `getChallengeResponse()`, so the claimed mismatch (and “can never validate”) isn’t supported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Used recovery codes are never consumed for federated users, allowing infinite code reuse

adjudication.rationale: In the federated user storage implementation added/extended by this diff, recovery codes are validated but never removed/updated after a successful use. Specifically, `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(... )` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)` without consuming the matched code or persisting an updated credential list. This enables repeated reuse of the same recovery code for federated users handled by this storage provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NPE in getCredentials for unknown user: getMyUser can return null and myUser.recoveryCodes is dereferenced without a null check

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)` (newly added), it does `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` and then immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` / `myUser.otp` without checking for `myUser == null`. Since `getMyUser` returns `users.get(translateUserName(user.getUsername()))`, it can return null for an unknown/unmapped user, leading to an NPE as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes stored in plaintext in user storage instead of SHA-256 hashes like local Keycloak storage

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces storing `generatedCodes` serialized directly as JSON into a `UserCredentialModel` and passing it to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` (CredentialHelper#createRecoveryCodesCredential). The test user storage implementation persists `input.getChallengeResponse()` as `credentialData` and validates by deserializing the stored list and doing direct string equality against the entered code (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage#updateCredential and #isValid). This demonstrates recovery codes are stored and compared in plaintext in user storage, unlike the typical hashed-at-rest approach used for credentials in local storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Optional.get() without presence check in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean causes NoSuchElementException/500 on login path

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the code assigns `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can return `Optional.empty()` when neither a federated nor local recovery-codes credential exists, which would trigger `NoSuchElementException` at runtime on this login bean path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated credential shadows a stale local credential with no reconciliation or warning, allowing the two stores to diverge

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a federated-first lookup for recovery codes (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(): checks getFederatedCredentialsStream() first, then falls back to local stored credentials). At the same time, CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential() will write to user storage via user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...) and, if that succeeds, it does not remove or reconcile any pre-existing local (Keycloak DB) recovery-codes credential. This allows both a federated and a local credential to coexist and silently diverge, with the local one effectively shadowed. If the federated credential is later removed/unavailable, the code will fall back to the stale local credential, potentially re-enabling old recovery codes unexpectedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuntimeException wrapping with no context on serialization failure after codes were shown to user, leaving codes never persisted

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, JSON serialization of `generatedCodes` is wrapped in a try/catch that rethrows `new RuntimeException(e)` with no message/context. If `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` throws, the method aborts before `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` or `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`, so recovery codes are not persisted. The diff doesn’t show user-facing handling, but the lack of contextual error makes debugging/diagnosis harder and can strand the flow on an internal error.
